reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present in operative text: a Vendor defend-and-indemnify obligation running to Licensee and its affiliates, the four required triggers (IP infringement of Licensed Technology/services/deliverables, breach of applicable law, Vendor-caused data incident, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), and the standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics.

The Customer-side indemnity in Article XII is narrowed exactly to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law, matching the preferred limitation; the two edits are targeted phrase replacements rather than a clause rewrite.

The carve-out from Article XIII is necessary, not extra: Article XIII(a) expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for infringement claims, so without the carve-out the new indemnity would be nullified. No hold-harmless language, extra indemnitees, Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics or fallback remedies were imported.

Fallback is not satisfied as a package (no modification/combination/specification exclusions, no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, no 3x annual-fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the locked preferred level is complete and the two levels are separate bargains.

Note for the rationale, not a deviation: the untouched opening words of Article XII ("Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights") remain and sit in tension with the narrowed indemnity; consider a follow-up trim if the counterparty reopens Article XII. Drafting in limb (ii) ("breach ... of any representation, warranty ... under applicable law") is slightly awkward but reads as breach of applicable law.
